transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text:
Hello! I'm Dora, and I've just completed your post-cataract surgery follow-up check. 

Do you have any questions about your surgery or your recovery?

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: Hi Dora! Yes, I do have a few questions. First, I'm wondering when I can start doing a little bit of gardening?

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text:
Great question! You can start doing light gardening after 1 week following your surgery. That's perfectly fine to do.

However, you'll want to avoid any heavy lifting or strenuous exercise for about a month after your operation.

Do you have any other questions?

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: Thank you for that advice! I also wanted to know when I can start using my eye gel for dry eyes?

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text:
That's a good question. If you were using eye gel for dry eyes before your surgery, it's safe to continue using it now, unless you've been told otherwise by your care team.

If you're unsure about the specific instructions for your eye gel, I'd recommend checking with your GP or the pharmacy.

Do you have any other questions?

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: Thanks, that helps a lot. I'm also feeling very sensitive to bright light. Is that normal?

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text:
Yes, some light sensitivity is quite normal as your eyes adjust to the new lenses. 

If it's mild and things just seem brighter than you're used to, I'd recommend wearing sunglasses when you're outside.

However, if you're experiencing significant pain in bright light, or if your eye is also red and painful, that's not normal and we may need to check that further. In that case, please let your care team know.

Do you have any other questions?

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: Got it, thanks for explaining. Lastly, should I still have some blurriness by now?

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text:
It's quite common to have some blurriness in the first week after surgery, and it should improve quickly and settle down over time.

However, I don't have your specific details, so I'm not sure exactly how long ago your surgery was. If your vision is still quite blurry or getting significantly worse, we may need to check it to make sure everything's okay.

Do you have any other questions?

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: No, that's all the questions I had for now. Thank you so much for your help!

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Wonderful! Just to confirm - have all your questions been answered today?

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: Yes, you've answered all my questions. Thanks again for your help!

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: You're very welcome! Take care, and best wishes with your recovery.

verdict.label: pass
